text:
maria: Ran a large nsys trace on staging-int8 pool — seeing a weird p95/p99 tail on the decoder for requests with ~1.5k tokens. Timeline attached, can someone eyeball?

ben: ping — can you paste the nsys command and a short TL;DR of what you saw in the timeline?

maria: nsys command I used: ```nsys profile -o /tmp/trace --sample=cpu --trace=cuda,cublas,cudnn --capture-range=nvtx --nvtx-attr=pid,tid -- python run_inference.py --model redwood-int8 --batch 32 --seq 1536``` Timeline: lots of nvtx spans around "decoder_step", then recurring bursts of `host_dequant` + `cudaMemcpy` immediately before the GPU quant-gemm kernels.

akshay: quick skim — that pattern screams host-side dequant/hostcopy serializing the GPU stream. Do we have a seq limit in the int8 kernel? I remember fallback to host for >1024.

maria: yes — int8 fused kernel (quant-kernel-v2) only supports max_seq=1024, so for longer sequences the runtime slices into a fallback path that does dequant on CPU and then memcpy to GPU. That's exactly where the spikes line up.

yana: also look at batching heuristics: current heuristic allows batches to grow up to 48 when avg_seq>512. So when a long-seq request enters, it creates a big batch and amplifies the host-dequant wall time. Might be a batching + kernel-support interaction.

akshay: extracted top ops from nsys (by CPU time): host_dequant: 18%, cudaMemcpyHostToDevice: 12%, runtime scheduling: 6%. By GPU time: quant-gemm: 44%, attention_fused: 22%. Host dequant is single-threaded and blocks completion events.

maria: uploaded perf traces and perfetto capture — perf-bot should have the link. I color-coded NVTX around the kernel fallback sequences.

perf-bot: nsys upload ready: https://perf.company/trace/1977654321 (contains nsys .qdrep + perfetto JSON) :mag: :rocket:

ben: two immediate mitigation ideas: 1) cap effective batch size for long-seq flows (reduce tail aggregation), 2) implement chunked int8 kernel (process seq in sub-chunks on-GPU to avoid host dequant). Which is faster to test?

akshay: cap batch size is trivial config change. Chunked kernel is more invasive but avoids host copy entirely. I'll prototype a tiled loop in the kernel that iterates over sequence chunks (e.g., 512) and keeps KV on-device. Risk: register pressure and kernel launch overhead.

maria: attached a perfetto screenshot showing repeated host memcpy spikes at t=12.2s, 12.8s, 13.5s — every decoder step after kv-miss. Also added a small kv_hitrate log for the run: kv_hitrate=0.32 overall, but client-specific sequences show cold-starts.

yana: small config proposed for staging A/B test to limit blast radius: ```runtime:
  max_batch_size: 32
  batch_timeout_ms: 6
  kv_warmup: true
  kv_prefetch_ratio: 0.2
  seq_limit_int8: 1024  # fallback threshold
``` This reduces long-seq batching while keeping short-seq throughput.

ben: also add per-request tagging to trace to correlate kernel fallback with user/caller type.

akshay: I'll try two runs: (A) cap batch size for seq>1024; (B) new chunked kernel that loops chunks of 512 and reuses KV on-device. Expect A to reduce p99 but increase tail token cost (more RT per token). B should remove host-dequant spikes but needs verification on throughput.

maria: created an experiment in console: int8-fallback-vs-chunking, 5% of traffic, run 6h. Collecting p95/p99 latency, token cost, and accuracy checks vs fp32.

perf-bot: scheduled perfjob #4821: int8-fallback vs kernel-chunking. Expected finish: ~6h. Results will include nsys + aggregated SLO metrics.

ben: long-term: prioritize adding unit tests that exercise sequence lengths >1024 to catch fallback regressions in CI. Also add regression alerting when host_dequant CPU% > 5% over a sliding window.

maria: ack — I'll add the CI trace test and the alert. Sharing a short checklist: 1) cap batching for long sequences (staging A), 2) prototype chunked kernel (akshay), 3) run perfjob, 4) add CI and alerting, 5) document kernel seq limits in runtime model catalog.

yana: sounds good. If chunked kernel works, consider a runtime knob to enable chunking vs fallback depending on hardware.

akshay: one more note — quant accuracy: chunking must preserve KV ordering and reduce numerical drift; we should run the evaluation harness to validate logits vs fp32 on a set of prompts (I will add that to the perfjob).

maria: thanks all, will follow up with perfjob outputs. If anyone wants early access to the perfetto link let me know. :thumbsup:
